findings.where: Guide body, the "Vibe" section heading (desktop and phone)
findings.fault: The heading is styled as a link: it is underlined, italic and in the link colour. It is plain text, so tapping it does nothing. It is also the only section heading styled this way, so it looks like a way into more about the vibe.
findings.who_objects: A backpacker on a phone who wants to know what the crowd is like would tap it expecting more detail or matching hostels. Nothing happens, and they learn not to trust which of the page's links are real.

findings.where: "Good for" section, all twelve tags (First-time surfers through Sunsets), desktop and phone
findings.fault: Each tag is drawn as a filled, outlined pill, which is how a filter chip looks. Only filters use that shape. The tags are static facts, so tapping one selects and filters nothing. On a hostel site where filtering by vibe is the product's main promise, they read as filters.
findings.who_objects: A backpacker on a hostel site expects tags like "Remote workers" or "Budget" to filter hostels. They tap them, nothing changes, and on a phone it can look as if the page is broken or still loading.

findings.where: The "launching across Indonesia, listings coming soon" notice below "What to look for" (desktop and phone)
findings.fault: The notice sits on a saturated red block, the colour of an error or danger state. It is a calm notice about Manta's launch, but it takes the error signifier, so it reads as a failure. The project's interior announcement uses the ink night ground for this.
findings.who_objects: A visitor skimming on a phone sees a red box at the end of the guide and assumes something failed, such as listings that won't load or a site error. This is the wrong impression on the one block that explains why there are no hostels.

findings.where: Top nav (wordmark, "Destinations", "How we rank") and footer ("Privacy", "Terms", "How we rank", "Report content")
findings.fault: Every link except the email address goes nowhere. The wordmark, "How we rank" in both places, "Privacy", "Terms" and "Report content" all point back to this same page. "Destinations" jumps to a #destinations anchor, but the page has no destinations section. A visitor cannot reach the home page, other destinations, the ranking method or the legal pages.
findings.who_objects: A backpacker who wants to compare Canggu with another Bali stop finds "Destinations" does nothing. A cautious first-time visitor who opens "How we rank" or "Privacy" to decide whether to trust a pre-launch site lands back where they started, which looks careless on a site that sells trust.

findings.where: End of the guide, the coming-soon notice
findings.fault: The page ends with no way forward. The notice says Canggu listings are coming soon but offers no next step: no way to hear when they launch and no link to destinations that are live. The guide is the visitor's last stop.
findings.who_objects: A backpacker who has just decided Canggu suits them reaches the end with no hostels and nothing to do next. They leave for another booking site and have no reason to come back.
